newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam awards army officers for fighting in north.
newsitem.headline: Saddam awards army officers for fighting in north.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein has decorated for bravery senior army commanders who fought alongside one Kurdish faction against a rival group in August, government newspapers reported on Tuesday.

Saddam was shown on state-run televison late on Monday decorating Defence Minister General Sultan Hashim Ahmed, his own son Qusi who was named as the Republican Guards' supervisor and senior commanders for their distinguished role in the fighting which led to the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) capturing the northern city of Arbil from its rivals in August.
Saddam did not mention directly the two Kurdish parties but he praised the KDP for its cooperation with Baghdad and lashed out at its rivals, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
"They fought against Iraq for the favour of Zionism (Israel), Iran and America," newspapers quoted Saddam as saying in reference to the PUK led by Jalal Talabani.

The Iraqi leader urged the PUK to set aside its differences with Baghdad, saying: "Even those deviationists, we wish them to turn back from their deviation...We wish them to return to their homeland after washing themselves from their shameless stands."

Baghdad's military backing of the KDP in August led to retaliatory missile strikes on southern Iraq by the United States which opposes any military involvement by the Iraqi government in the north of its country.

"They (Americans) have become just like children, they want to commit aggression against us every day because the White House does not like Baghdad which was built before the (U.S) became a state," Saddam said.

The United States has sponsored two rounds of peace talks with the warring Kurdish factions which agreed to a ceasefire. Iraq opposed the U.S. efforts and urged the Kurdish leaders to come to Baghdad for talks.
